If y fills up with all those higher-ranked applicants, I'll be rejected. Then I'll propose to z, where I'm ranked 1st. If z also fills up quickly, I'll be rejected again. Given the popularity of y, and my relatively low priority at y, I need to ensure I have a viable path to z. Ranking w or x higher than z would reduce my chances of getting into z if y doesn't work out. Since most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, x and w will likely have slots available longer than y or z.

Therefore, sticking to my true preferences is the best strategy to maximize my chances of getting matched to either y or z. I don't want to risk being stuck with x as my only option by ranking it higher, as I'd rather be unmatched than go to x.
